ledger.note: 1292: Peureulak is united with Pasai. Infobox of the Peureulak page 'Disestablished: 1292'; 'Perlak was united with the Samudera Pasai Kingdom' after the last sultan died, under Muhammad Malik Al Zahir, son of Al Malik al-Saleh. The page gives no month and no boundary; The page names only 'what is now the East Aceh Regency'; the region is the researcher's reading, a 45 km circle round Langsa clipped to Aceh province (reviewer fix: the earlier 70 km circle reached Langkat and Aceh Tamiang). The year 1292 comes from the infobox 'Disestablished: 1292'; the union sentence itself is undated.

1350: a Majapahit fleet raids Pasai. The Majapahit page cites the Hikayat Raja Pasai, which 'describes a Majapahit naval invasion on the Samudera Pasai Sultanate' in 1350; the Pasai page: 'Majapahit attacked and looted the place in the middle of the 14th century'. No ground is said to be held.

1350: the raid ends; neither page says the invaders stayed. Pasai's ruler list runs on (Malik Salahuddin 1340-1355, Malikuzzahir 1360-1369). The Majapahit dossier carries the tributary tint from 1350 to 1406.

region.text: the Pasai coast of north Sumatra

ledger.note: 1350: Pasai enters Majapahit's tributary sphere (mirror of majapahit /ledger/5). The year is the Majapahit page's naval invasion of 1350 (Hikayat Raja Pasai); neither it nor the Pasai page ('attacked and looted the place in the middle of the 14th century') calls Pasai a vassal or says Majapahit stayed. The tint rests on that raid and on the Nagarakretagama (written 1365), which lists 'Samudra (Samudra Pasai)' and 'negara Perlak' among the Sumatran places the king claimed authority over, claims the page does not say were enforced (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nagarakretagama).

region.text: the Pasai coast of north Sumatra

ledger.note: 1406: the tint ends with the Regreg War (mirror of majapahit /ledger/20). The Regreg War page says 'overseas possessions outside of Java have liberated themselves' and names Palembang, Malayu, Malacca and Brunei but neither Pasai nor a year for each; 1406 is the war's last year. Pasai's own list has Sultanah Nahrasiyah from 1406 ('Glory period of Samudra Pasai').
1521: the Portuguese occupy Pasai. 'The Portuguese occupied Pasai in 1521, 10 years after their conquest of Malacca'; infobox 'Portuguese invasion: 1521'.
1524: the Portuguese garrison leaves. 'The Portuguese garrison evacuated Pasai in 1524.'

ledger.note: 1524: Aceh annexes Pasai. After the Portuguese left, 'the first Sultan of Aceh, Ali Mughayat Syah' annexed the territory; infobox 'Conquered by the Aceh Sultanate: 1524'. The Aceh page says only that his conquests 'included Deli, Pedir, and Pasai'. Cliopatria ends Pasai in 1520 and grows Aceh in 1526. Second page: the Ali Mughayat Syah page has 'the conquest of neighboring Daya (1520), Pidie (1521), and Pasai (1524)' and 'in 1524 Pasai was eventually captured and the Portuguese garrison there was expelled' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ali_Mughayat_Syah), so two pages agree on 1524.

wars.name: Majapahit invasion of Samudera Pasai
wars.outcome: Pasai attacked and looted by Majapahit's fleet (four hundred large jong ships per the Hikayat Raja Pasai); no annexation is stated.
wars.note: The Pasai page gives no year, only 'the middle of the 14th century'. The Majapahit raid is mirrored in the ledger as the tributary tint /ledger vassal_start 1350 to vassal_end 1406.

wars.name: Campaign against Tamiang
wars.outcome: The ruler list notes that Malik Salahuddin (1340-1355) 'Attacked the Karang Baru Kingdom, Tamiang'; no territorial result is given.

wars.name: Majapahit attack on Pasai (1390s)
wars.outcome: No land is said to change hands: the ruler table only notes 'Attacked by Majapahit' against Sultan Zainal Abidin I (1394-1400).
wars.note: The table gives the reign, not the year of the attack, and no Majapahit page opened (Majapahit, Regreg War) mentions it; the years 1394-1400 are the reign's, not the attack's. Majapahit sacked Singapura in 1398 (Majapahit dossier), which may be the same naval effort; unverified.

wars.name: Portuguese occupation of Pasai
wars.outcome: The Portuguese occupied Pasai from 1521 and evacuated their garrison in 1524.

wars.name: Aceh conquest of Pasai
wars.outcome: Ali Mughayat Syah's conquests: 'the conquest of neighboring Daya (1520), Pidie (1521), and Pasai (1524)'; 'in 1524 Pasai was eventually captured and the Portuguese garrison there was expelled' (Ali Mughayat Syah page).
wars.note: Resolved in the review round: the Ali Mughayat Syah page dates the capture of Pasai to 1524, as the Pasai page does (which says the garrison 'evacuated'; this page says 'expelled'). The Aceh Sultanate page dates nothing for Pasai.

certainty.note: A coastal sultanate of the north Sumatran river mouths: no surveyed line; the eastern frontier with Peureulak vanishes in 1292.

notes:
CLIOPATRIA vs THE PAGES. (1) The row runs 1272-1520; the page has the foundation in 1267, the Portuguese in 1521-1524 and Aceh's annexation in 1524, so the dossier runs 1267-1524 with new keyframes 1267, 1352 and 1521. (2) Cliopatria has no Pasai shape in 1352-1362 and draws Majapahit over the same cells; the pages describe a raid in 1350 ('attacked and looted'), not an annexation, so Pasai is kept and the Majapahit dossier tints it as a tributary 1350-1406. (3) Peureulak (East Aceh) joined Pasai in 1292 on the Peureulak page; it lies outside Cliopatria's outline and is added from 1292 (keyframe samudera-pasai-sultanate_1292 and every later keyframe), drawn as a 45 km circle round Langsa clipped to Aceh province; whether Peureulak stayed in Pasai to 1524 is not stated. (4) The Aceh Sultanate page does not date the annexation ('His conquests included Deli, Pedir, and Pasai'); 1524 is the Pasai page's and, in the review round, also the Ali Mughayat Syah page's ('the conquest of neighboring ... Pasai (1524)'). Cliopatria's Aceh row has 23 cells beside Pasai in 1516-1525 and takes Pasai's cells in 1526.

AREA: no infobox area on the Pasai page (Cliopatria 8,216-8,675 km2).

NOT SETTLED: the Pasai ruler list has gaps (1355-1360, 1389-1394, 1400-1406, 1517-1524) and the 1360/69-1380/89 entry is a range; Marco Polo's 'Ferlec' is not dated on the page; Tamiang campaign undated. Peureulak (840-1292) needs a dossier: peureulak-sultanate (group se-02). Portuguese Malacca's role in the 1521 occupation is not on the page.

PAGE BUDGET (5): Samudera Pasai Sultanate, Aceh Sultanate, Peureulak Sultanate, and the Majapahit page (shared with the Majapahit dossier) = 4; not opened: Hikayat Raja Pasai, Ferlec/Marco Polo, Portuguese Malacca. Gazetteer: 'Langsa' (place) stands for Peureulak; the gazetteer lacks Peureulak, Pasai, Samudera.

REVIEW ROUND (2026-10-19, author fixes). (a) Keyframe _1272 is now verdict ok (shape as drawn, 1272-1291) and the Peureulak union starts with the new keyframe _1292 (1292-1351), so the keyframes agree with /ledger gain 1292. (b) Peureulak is drawn as {intersect: Langsa 45 km, admin1 Aceh}: the gazetteer puts Langsa at 4.67 N 97.97 E (the real city is at about 4.47 N), so at the gazetteer's coordinate the Aceh clip cuts nothing and the circle's bbox is 97.61-98.13 E, 4.30-4.91 N (13 cells, 3,288 km2); if the gazetteer corrects Langsa the clip will matter. Gazetteer note: the Langsa latitude looks wrong by about 0.2 degrees. (c) Added vassal_start 1350 (confidence 2) and vassal_end 1406 (confidence 1) with counterpart majapahit, mirroring the Majapahit dossier. I partly disagree with the tint itself: the Majapahit page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Majapahit) and the Pasai page describe a raid ('attacked and looted'), not tribute; only the Nagarakretagama's list of claimed places (canto 13: Samudra Pasai, Perlak; written 1365) supports a tint, and the Nagarakretagama page says the claims are not shown to have been enforced. The events are kept so the two dossiers agree; a rendering agent that wants conservatism can draw Pasai untinted. (d) Added the war 'Majapahit attack on Pasai (1390s)' with empty zones. (e) The thin item /ledger 1524 is settled with a second page (Ali Mughayat Syah). Not opened: Hikayat Raja Pasai, Marco Polo's Ferlec.
